blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies. We introduce OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on each robot's kinematics in a specific scene to produce embodiment-specific behavior. This kinematic graph represents the robot's joint positions, motion axes, and connectivity to its visual observation, allowing the policy to account for how its embodiment related to objects and surfaces in the scene. A flow-matching policy predicts relative joint motions for each node, enabling control across robots with different degrees of freedom and kinematic configurations. To learn how physical structure shapes behavior at scale, we procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible robot embodiments; next, we develop algorithms to generate robot trajectories in simulation for all embodiments; finally, we train across diverse simulated manipulation tasks. On 2,000 embodiment-scene-held-out evaluation episodes, OmniAct achieves 63.0% success, compared to 17.8% for pi 0.5 and 57.9% for the strongest baseline; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it achieves 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra's 41.1%. On a previously unseen real-world robot, it achieves nearly twice the success rate of the next best method, MolmoAct2. Beyond task success, we observe that OmniAct learns distinct manipulation strategies that exploit the capabilities and accommodate the limitations of different morphologies. Project: https://omniact.github.io/

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: A single policy capable of controlling robots with diverse embodiments must solve two related problems: transferring task knowledge across robots and adapting behavior to each robot’s physical capabilities . Existing approaches have made substantial progress on the former by identifying representations and interfaces that can be shared across embodiments. Generalist vision-language-action models use shared end-effector commands, unified action tokenizers, or learned action latents [ 9 , 36 , 21 , 27 , 4 ] . Object-centric methods represent desired object motions or interactions that can be transferred between robots [ 3 , 44 , 18 , 25 ] . These approaches facilitate transfer by exploiting commonalities across embodiments. However, transferring task knowledge does not necessarily lead to effective control of each robot. Two robots pursuing the same goal may require different grasps, trajectories, or contact strategies because of differences in their kinematics, workspace, and dexterity.
blocks.zh: 单一的政策能够控制具有多种表现形式的机器人,必须解决两个相关的问题:将任务知识传递给机器人,并使行为适应每个机器人的身体能力。 现有做法在前者方面取得了实质性进展,确定了可在各种表现上共享的表述和界面。 通用视觉-语言-行动模型使用共享的终端效应指令,统一的动作示意剂,或学到的动作潜伏[9,36,21,27,4]. 以物体为中心的方法代表理想的物体运动或机器人之间可以转移的相互作用[3,44,18,25]. 这些办法通过利用各种表现的共同点,促进转让。 然而,转移任务知识并不一定导致对每个机器人的有效控制. 两个追求同一目标的机器人可能因其运动力,工作空间,和弹性的不同而需要不同的抓取,轨迹,或接触策略.

blocks.en:
Learning embodiment-specific behaviors presents several challenges. First , a policy must reason about the robot’s geometry in relation to the observed scene. The usefulness of a joint configuration depends on where its joints and motion axes lie relative to the objects and obstacles it must interact with.
Existing policies incorporate descriptions such as URDFs or kinematic graphs, but often encode the robot independently of the scene [ 7 , 32 , 35 ] . Second , the policy must accommodate different kinematic structures, including variations in joint types, degrees of freedom, and link topology, while still supporting a common control interface. Existing approaches have demonstrated transfer across relatively small collections of manipulators [ 47 , 39 , 28 ] . Third , the policy must learn how changes in morphology affect behavior so that it can control embodiments not encountered during training. This requires experience across a sufficiently diverse set of physical structures. Prior efforts to scale learning across hundreds of morphologies have primarily focused on locomotion [ 1 , 15 ] and not manipulation.
blocks.zh:
学习具体表现的行为提出了若干挑战。 首先,政策必须说明机器人与所观测场景的几何关系。 联合配置的效用取决于其关节和运动轴相对于它必须与之互动的物体和障碍的位置.
现有政策包含了URDF或动画图等描述,但经常将机器人独立于场景编码[7,32,35]. 第二,该政策必须适应不同的运动结构,包括联合类型、自由度和连接地形的不同,同时仍然支持共同的控制界面。 现有做法表明,在相对较少的操纵者集合体之间转移[47、39、28]。 第三,政策必须了解形态学的变化如何影响行为,以便控制训练期间没有遇到的表征。 这就需要拥有足够多样的物理结构的经验。 以前在数百种形态学中扩大学习范围的努力主要集中于运动[1,15]而不是操纵.

blocks.en:
We introduce OmniAct , a policy trained across one million embodiments, capable of adapting behavior to each embodiment and what it can achieve in a given scene.
Our approach represents each robot through a scene-grounded kinematic graph , expressing its joint geometry in the 3D coordinate frame of each observing camera. Each joint and fingertip is represented as a node containing its camera-frame position, motion axis, joint type, proprioceptive state, and kinematic connectivity. This allows the policy to relate the robot’s physical structure to the corresponding visual observations.
We pair this representation with a variable-DoF action representation that jointly predicts relative joint motions and end-effector pose updates using a flow-matching policy. By unifying the indexing scheme across all embodiments, our model learn to support different numbers and configurations of joints within the same network.
These two components allow the policy to generate motions directly from each robot’s kinematic structure and its relationship to the scene.

blocks.en:
Training a policy to exploit these differences requires substantial diversity in robot morphology. A policy trained on a handful of embodiments may learn effective manipulation strategies for those robots without learning how to adapt them to new ones.
We develop a procedure to instantiate one million unique robot embodiments and create algorithms to automatically generate trajectories for each of them in simulation.
Our data generation pipeline varies joint configurations, link geometry, and kinematic topology to generate embodiments; we use inverse-kinematics screening and physics-based acceptance to ensure feasibility of each trajectory. The resulting training distribution exposes the policy to a broad range of robot configurations and allow us to test on unseen embodiments.

blocks.en:
We evaluate OmniAct on embodiments and scenes held out from training. On OmniAct-Bench , it succeeds in 63.0% of episodes within 500 steps, against 57.9% for the strongest baseline and 17.8% for π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it reaches 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra’s 41.1% at the same step budget and 54.8% with twice the budget ( Table 3 ). On a real OpenYAM arm with a fine-tip
gripper, neither seen in training, OmniAct completes 13 of 20 pick-and-place trials. The only baseline to succeed at all is MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM, for which this arm is in distribution, at 7 of 20; every other baseline completes none ( Table 5 ). We observe that on this arm the policy sometimes makes use
of the long final link specific to this unseen embodiment, extending it horizontally and then rotating the gripper to reach
far targets ( Section 3.4 ), a behavior not seen from MolmoAct2 trained exclusively on YAM. These results suggest that policies grounded in a robot’s kinematics are a path towards better cross-embodiment generalization.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: We introduce OmniAct , a single policy that learns cross-embodiment manipulation across robots with different kinematic structures. Our approach has three components. First, we represent each robot through a scene-grounded kinematic graph that expresses its geometry in the coordinate frame of its visual observations. Second, we develop a variable-DoF action representation that jointly predicts joint motions and end-effector poses across different robot configurations. Third, we generate diverse embodiments and collect successful manipulation trajectories in simulation to train the policy across one million robots.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了Omni Act(Omni Act), 一项单一的政策是学习不同运动结构的机器人的交叉化操纵. 我们的方法有三个组成部分。 首先,我们通过一个场景定位的动能图来代表每个机器人,在它的视觉观测坐标框中表达它的几何特征. 其次,我们开发了一个可变的 DoF 动作代表,共同预测不同机器人配置的联动和终端效应器. 第三,我们在模拟中产生多种化身,收集成功的操纵轨迹,以训练100万机器人的政策。

blocks.en:
We decompose each robot into nodes representing arm joints, gripper drivers, gripper tips, and annotated points such as the tool center point (TCP). Each node n n has a type τ n ∈ { terminal , revolute , prismatic , point } \tau_{n}\in\{\mathrm{terminal},\mathrm{revolute},\mathrm{prismatic},\mathrm{point}\} and an actuation indicator that distinguishes driven joints, terminal joints, and annotated points. The kinematic topology is encoded through shortest-path distances between nodes, which enter the Transformer as attention biases [ 43 ] .
Nodes are ordered according to their kinematic structure and left-padded to a maximum supported node count, keeping end-effector nodes at the final positions of the sequence. This provides a consistent indexing scheme across different embodiments while preserving their variable numbers of joints.

blocks.zh: 几何定位在相机的3D坐标框中进行。 我们没有明确将联合位置投射成图像像素或预测地点的图像样本。 共享的视角和视图嵌入提供了几何符号和视觉符号之间的对应,而变形器则学习其相互作用.

blocks.en: 2.2 Variable-DoF Action Prediction
blocks.zh: 2.2 可变行动预测

blocks.en: Robots differ in their numbers of joints, joint types, and available motion directions. We use a node-aligned action representation in which the output follows the same padded ordering as the input kinematic graph. This allows a single network to predict actions for different embodiments while maintaining correspondence between each node’s geometry and its control signals.
blocks.zh: 机器人在关节数量,关节类型,以及可用的运动方向上都有所不同. 我们使用一个节点对齐的动作表示,其中输出遵循与输入动图相同的加序. 这使得一个单一的网络能够预测不同表现的动作,同时保持每个节点几何及其控制信号之间的对应.

blocks.en: Each output node is processed by two prediction heads: a relative joint-motion head and a relative pose head. The joint-motion head predicts changes in the robot’s joint coordinates, while the pose head predicts relative EE poses associated with the corresponding end-effector nodes. Both heads are trained through flow matching, and both predictions contribute to the control executed by the robot.
blocks.zh: 每个输出节点由两个预测头处理:相对的关节动头和相对的姿势头. 联合运动头会预测机器人联合坐标的变化,而姿势头会预测相对的EE姿态与相应的终端效应节点相关. 两个头部都通过流匹配来训练,两个预测都有助于机器人执行的控制.

blocks.en: We normalize joint actions using empirical statistics associated with their left-padded node slots, which we find effective for representing diverse embodiments. Action outputs are masked according to the valid nodes and action quantities for each robot.
blocks.zh: 我们利用与它们左插点插点有关的实证统计数据,使联合行动正常化,我们发现它们能够有效地代表各种表现形式。 动作输出根据每个机器人的有效节点和行动数量进行遮掩.

blocks.en: 2.3 Scaling Embodiments
blocks.zh: 2.3 放大浮雕

blocks.en:
A policy trained on a small set of robots may learn manipulation strategies specific to those kinematics, limiting its ability to adapt to unfamiliar embodiments. We therefore procedurally generate one million robot embodiments spanning different kinematic structures, joint configurations, and link geometries.
Each embodiment is generated deterministically from a random seed, generating its morphology, joint limits, actuator dynamics, link geometry, inertia, and appearance. This makes each robot reproducible without separately storing its complete description.
blocks.zh:
一项对一小批机器人进行培训的政策可能学习专门针对这些动能分子的操纵策略,限制其适应不熟悉的化身的能力。 因此,我们从程序上创造了100万个机器人的化身,它们跨越不同的运动结构、联合配置和连接地理美图。
每个表征都是由随机的种子产生,产生其形态,联合极限,动因动力学,联系几何,惯性,外观. 这使得每个机器人在不单独存储其完整描述的情况下可以复制.

blocks.en: We filter generated candidates for self-collision and grasp feasibility. Grasp feasibility is evaluated by solving inverse kinematics for representative target grasp poses on randomly sampled objects. 84.4% of all generated embodiments fail self-collision and 97.5% of the surviving embodiments fail grasp checks despite being sampled from distributions designed to produce realistic robots. 6-DoF, 7-DoF, and 8-DoF embodiments have pass rates of 0.016%, 0.299%, and 0.653% overall pass rate. Filtering these candidates avoids expensive trajectory collection for embodiments that cannot perform simple manipulation tasks.
blocks.zh: 我们筛选了自我整合的候选者,并掌握了可行性。 格拉斯普的可行性是通过在随机抽样的物体上解决具有代表性的目标抓取的反动因子来评估的。 在所有产生的浮雕中,有84.4%的浮雕自失能,97.5%的幸存浮雕自失能检查,尽管从旨在生产现实机器人的分布中取样。 6-DOF、7-DOF和8-DOF的通过率分别为0.016%、0.299%和0.653%。 过滤这些候选人可以避免昂贵的轨迹收集,用于无法执行简单操纵任务的浮雕.

blocks.en: We collect manipulation trajectories in MolmoSpaces [ 22 ] , instantiating each feasible embodiment in randomly generated scenes with different tasks and initial configurations. We plan two scene-task instances per embodiment.
blocks.zh: 我们收集MolmoSpaces的操纵轨迹[22],即时将每一个可行的浮现在随机生成的场景中,具有不同的任务和初始配置. 我们计划每个化身有两个场景任务

blocks.en: Trajectory generation uses a planner that proposes locally feasible motions under the current robot’s kinematic constraints. At each step, the planner considers feasible immediate motions towards the next desired pose [ 22 ] without explicitly planning an embodiment-specific long-horizon strategy. Different from MolmoSpaces’ use of top-down poses calculated assuming the Franka robot, we randomly rotate the grasp poses and allow for any kinematically feasible pose on the robot to form the support. We filter for successful episodes, producing demonstrations of manipulation behaviors that are feasible for each robot. 6-, 7-, and 8-DoF embodiments have flat episode success rates of 35.9%, 34.8%, and 36.4%, compared to embodiment screening’s DoF-dependent pass rates. Successful episodes are stored with sufficient simulation state to reconstruct the environment at intermediate steps. Table 1 summarizes the resulting corpus.
blocks.zh: 轨迹生成使用一个在目前机器人的运动限制下提出当地可行的运动的计程器. 在每一步骤,规划者都考虑立即提出可行的动议,以实现下一个理想的姿势[22],而没有明确规划具体体现的长远战略。 与MolmoSpaces使用自上而下的假设 Franka 机器人的姿势不同, 我们随机旋转了抓住的姿势, 并允许机器人上任何动能可行的姿势组成支持。 我们过滤成功的事件, 产生每个机器人都可行的操纵行为。 6-、7-和8-DoF的配音成功率是35.9%、34.8%和36.4%,而配音检查的配音合格率是DoF。 成功的事件保存在足够的模拟状态下,以便在中间步骤重建环境. 表1汇总了由此而来的数据。

blocks.en: A fixed-seed RNG is used to reproducibly hold out 5% of embodiments and, within each task, 5% of scenes. A trajectory is used for training only if neither its embodiment nor its scene is reserved. An embodiment or scene is called seen when it appears in at least one accepted training trajectory. After this procedure, 18.3% of embodiments and 10.9% of scenes end up unseen from training, directly or indirectly. 14.5% of all trajectories are comprised of both unseen embodiments and unseen scenes. The subset with both embodiment and scenes unseen is denoted OmniAct-Bench , used for benchmarking.

blocks.en: The key takeaways are as follows: (a) In simulation on robots seen to baselines, OmniAct performs better or on par with existing methods despite not seeing the robot itself; (b) In simulation on unseen robots, OmniAct outperforms all baseline methods, including embodiment-specific and embodiment-agnostic policies, as well as the generalist VLM GPT-6 Astra, despite a smaller step budget; (c) In real-world deployment, OmniAct performs better or on par with existing methods on robots these existing methods specialize towards; (d) OmniAct adapts its motion strategy based on the embodiment and the task at hand, instead of retargeting one canonical grasp across bodies.
blocks.zh: 主要外购如下:(a) 在模拟被视为基线的机器人时,OmniAct尽管没有看到机器人本身,但表现更好或与现有方法相当;(b) 在模拟看不见的机器人时,OmniAct超越了所有基线方法,包括具体化和隐形的不可知性政策,以及通论者VLM GPT-6 Astra,尽管其步骤预算较小;(c) 在现实世界部署中,OmniAct更好地或与现有方法相同地执行这些专门面向机器人的方法;(d) OmniAct根据嵌入和手头的任务调整其运动战略,而不是重新瞄准一个横跨各机构的控制。

blocks.en: Training data. We train on our corpus of 1M procedurally generated manipulators ( Section 2.3 ) performing manipulation in MolmoSpaces scenes [ 22 ] .
blocks.zh: 培训数据。 我们在MolmoSpaces场景中训练1M程序产生的操纵器(第2.3节)[22]。

blocks.en: Baselines. We compare with frontier policies including π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} [ 19 ] , DreamZero [ 42 ] , MolmoAct2 [ 13 ] , GPT-6 Astra (max thinking), and embodiment generalization specialists UMI [ 8 ] and UMI-on-Air [ 16 ] . To address the possibility that a multi-view setup would provide better visual context compared to UMI’s single-view setup, we add a variant of UMI supplied with a 3-view camera setup as another baseline. We train UMI on the same simulated trajectories as our training but with UMI’s setup, to measure the effects of our architectural choices that facilitate our specific input conditioning ( Section 2.1 ). In real-world deployment, we additionally measure LAP-3B [ 45 ] , a zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer model, at their released checkpoint.
blocks.zh: 基线。 我们比较了前沿政策,包括 π 0.5\pi_{0.5} [19], DreamZero [42], Molmo Act2 [13], GPT-6 Astra (最大思考), 和 化身通用化专家 UMI [8] 和 UMI-on-Air [16]. 与UMI的单视图设置相比, 多视图设置会提供更好的视觉环境, 为了解决这种可能性, 我们增加了一个UMI的变体, 我们用同样的模拟轨迹来训练UMI, 在现实世界的部署中,我们额外测量了LAP-3B[45],这是在他们被释放的检查站进行的零射交叉化转移模型.

blocks.en: Benchmarks. We evaluate policies in three settings: i) on the existing MolmoSpaces benchmark that uses a robot that is in-distribution for the baseline policies, ii) on OmniAct-Bench , our benchmark based on held-out training data so unseen to all policies, and iii) on real-world tasks.
blocks.zh: 基准。 我们在三种情况下评价政策:(一) 现有的MolmoSpaces基准,该基准使用一个用于基线政策的机器人;(二) OmniAct-Bench基准,该基准基于所有政策所未见的搁置培训数据;(三) 现实世界的任务。

blocks.en: Implementation details. OmniAct is a 400M-parameter flow-matching policy over a fixed 12-slot node and action layout. It observes RGB views encoded by a frozen SigLIP 2 image encoder [ 38 ] , language encoded by the frozen text backbone of Qwen2.5-VL [ 2 ] , and the per-node embodiment representation of Section 2.1 . Training samples are 32-frame windows with a 31-step action prediction horizon. We train with an effective batch size of 128 with a learning rate of 10 − 3 10^{-3} for 520K steps. At evaluation the policy predicts a 31-step chunk and executes the first 8 steps every chunk.
blocks.zh: 执行细节。 OmniAct是一个固定的12slot节点和动作布局上的400M参数流量匹配政策. 它观察到由冻结的SigLIP 2图像编码器编码的RGB视图[38],由冻结的Qwen2.5-VL[2]文本主干体编码的语言,以及第2.1节的每个节点的体现. 培训样本为32帧窗口,具有31步动作预测视野. 我们的训练有效批量尺寸为128人,学习率为10 - 3 10 - 3 = 520K步。 在评价时,政策预测一个31步的块,每块执行前8步。

blocks.en: 3.1 Evaluation on seen robots in simulation
blocks.zh: 3.1 评价模拟中看到的机器人

blocks.en: We evaluate OmniAct in simulation on the MolmoSpaces benchmark, which uses the Franka Panda in the DROID configuration. All baselines have seen the Franka robot during training, whereas OmniAct does not.
blocks.zh: 我们在模拟MolmoSpaces基准时评价Omni Act,该基准在DROID配置中使用了Franka Panda. 所有基线在训练期间都看到Franka机器人,而OmniAct则没有.

blocks.en: OmniAct performs on par with embodiment-specialized models on their expert embodiments. Table 2 (full scenes) reports success on 2,622 2{,}622 held-out episodes under the same 500 500 -step cap. OmniAct reaches 69.1 % 69.1\% overall, against 63.0 % 63.0\% for MolmoBot and under 30 % 30\% for the DROID-trained policies, and leads on four of the six task families, with the largest margins where the task constrains placement or approach: for example, + 15.5 +15.5 percentage points over MolmoBot on placing next to a reference object.
blocks.zh: 《Omni Act》在专家的模范上与雕塑专业模型一样。 表2(完整场景)报告在同样500-500步封顶下的2,622个被搁置的片段取得了成功. 《OmniAct》总体达到69.1% 69.1% ,而MolmoBot为63.0% 63.0 %,DROID训练政策低于30% 30 % ,它领导了6个任务家庭中的4个,任务限制安置或方法的幅度最大:例如,在MolmoBot旁边放置一个参考对象时,比MolmoBot高出15.5+15.5个百分点。

blocks.en: OmniAct is robust against changes in object, lighting, and prompt format, and handles changes in camera and robot pose about as well as baselines. π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} and MolmoAct2 both score below their MolmoSpaces’ reported success. To understand this difference, we notice that MolmoSpaces’ scenes, especially the ones involving locating an object, have increased in difficulty since release [ 11 ] . We thus label our benchmark as Table 2 (full scenes) and contrast with Table 2 (simple scenes). Other than adding harder pick objects and tasks, the change also includes more diverse and randomized lighting, camera, robot pose, and prompt. To find out why π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} and MolmoAct2 drop in performance, we gradually change each of the variables in the Pick task and contrast the results with OmniAct in Figure 3 , which shows that OmniAct fluctuates within error margins while π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} and MolmoAct2 drop.
blocks.zh: OmniAct针对物体、照明和即时格式的变化是强有力的,它处理相机和机器人的改变以及基线。 MolmoAct2的得分都低于他们报告的成功率。 为了了解这一差异,我们注意到,MolmoSpaces的场景,特别是涉及确定物体位置的场景,自发布以来增加了困难。 因此,我们把基准标为表2(完整场景),与表2(简单场景)相对照。 除了增加更硬的采摘对象和任务外,这种改变还包括更加多样和随机化的照明,相机,机器人姿势,以及迅速. 为了找出为什么 ^ 0.5\pi_{0.5}和 MolmoAct2 的性能下降,我们逐渐改变 Pick 任务中的每个变量,并将结果与 OmniAct 在图 3 中对比,该图显示 OmniAct 在错误边距内波动,而 ^ 0.5\pi_{0.5}和 MolmoAct2 下降.

blocks.en: 3.2 Evaluation on unseen robots in simulation
blocks.zh: 3.2 在模拟中评价看不见的机器人

blocks.en: Next we want to test how well baseline methods generalize to novel embodiments. We use the held-out OmniAct-Bench benchmark ( Section 2.3 ).
blocks.zh: 接下来,我们要测试基线方法对新表现的概括程度。 我们使用被搁置的Omni Act-Bench基准(第2.3节)。

blocks.en: OmniAct generalizes to unseen embodiments in simulation. Rollout success on a random subset of 2000 episodes sampled from our benchmark is reported in Table 3 . From the results, we can see that OmniAct outperforms baselines at the same number of rollout steps, leading on six task families, and its overall success rate of 63.0% is 5.1 percentage points above the next best method, UMI with all camera views. Beyond policies, the general-purpose GPT-6 Astra model also struggles with random embodiments, trailing OmniAct by 23.6 percentage points at the same step count on the task families both were evaluated on (41.1% vs. 64.7%). We empirically observe that GPT-6 Astra, thanks to its language and multimodal reasoning capabilities, persistently retries with different solutions; however, even at double the step count, it is still behind OmniAct by 9.9 percentage points.
blocks.zh: Omni Act在模拟中一般化为看不见的化身. 从我们的基准中抽取的2000集随机子集的推出成功情况见表3。 从结果来看,我们可以看到OmniAct在同样数量的推出步骤上超越了基线,领先于6个任务家庭,其总的成功率为63.0%,比次佳方法(UMI)高出5.1个百分点,所有摄像头都能看到. 除了政策外,通用的GPT-6 Astra模型也与随机的表征相搏斗,在同一步骤中比Omni Act低23.6%,对任务家庭的评价均是41.1%对64.7%。 我们从经验上观察到,GPT-6 Astra由于其语言和多式联运推理能力,不断用不同的解决方案进行反复竞争;然而,即便在分数的两倍,它仍然落后于Omni Act9.9个百分点.

blocks.en: 3.3 Evaluation on real robots
blocks.zh: 3.3 对真正机器人的评价

blocks.en: We deploy OmniAct on two physical arms without fine-tuning: a Franka Panda, the robot every baseline was trained on, and an OpenYAM arm, which only MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM has trained on and which carries a fine-tip flange gripper that no policy has seen.
blocks.zh: 在两只没有微调的手臂上部署Omni Act:一只Franka熊猫,每个基线的机器人都受过训练,还有一只OpenYAM手臂,只有MolmoAct2-BimmanualYAM受过训练,它搭载了一个没有政策所见的精细的法兰格抓手。

blocks.en: Franka. We deploy on Franka Panda in the DROID configuration, the robot on which every baseline is also trained. For the MolmoAct2 baseline, its DROID-specific variant is deployed to ensure maximum compatibility.
blocks.zh: 法兰卡 我们在DROID的配置中部署Franka Panda, 每一个基线都用来训练的机器人。 对于MolmoAct2基线,其DROID特定变体被部署以确保最大兼容性.

blocks.en: OpenYAM. We next deploy on a physical OpenYAM arm fitted with its fine-tip flange gripper. For the MolmoAct2 baseline, the BimanualYAM variant is deployed and both YAM arms are enabled with their standard camera setup to comply with its model’s expectation.
blocks.zh: OpenYAM (英语). 接下来,我们部署 在物理 OpenYAM 臂 配备它的精细的Flange抓。 就MolmoAct2基线而言,采用了BimanualYAM的变体,并使YAM两款武器都能够安装符合模型预期的标准摄像机。

blocks.en: OpenYAM is in a relatively low-density region of our training data, and its fine-tip flange gripper is not seen during training. Table 4 and Figure 4 show that many of its key characteristics lie beyond the 5th/95th percentile.
blocks.zh: OpenYAM位于我们训练数据密度相对较低的区域,在训练期间看不到其精细的法兰格抓手. 表4和图4显示,其许多关键特征都超过了第5/95百分率。

blocks.en: On real unseen robots, OmniAct outperforms other models not specialized to the embodiment, and is on par with embodient-specialized models. We measure the success rate on an object pick-and-place task, varying the location of the object and the target within and at the boundary of the embodiment’s reach. We measure 20 starting setups per robot; in each setup, every policy starts from the same object positions, under a 1000 1000 step horizon ( Table 5 ). OmniAct is deployed zero-shot; it receives no fine-tuning on either robot, real or simulated.
blocks.zh: 在真正看不见的机器人上,Omni Act的性能超过了其他不专门用于化身的模型,并且与化身化专业模型处于同等地位. 我们测量一个物体选址任务的成功率, 改变物体的位置, 以及浮雕所到达的边界。 我们测量每个机器人的20个启动设置;在每一个设置中,每个策略都从同一个对象位置开始,在1000步的视野下(表5). OmniAct被部署为零镜头;无论是真实的还是模拟的机器人都得不到微调.

blocks.en: On Franka, OmniAct succeeds on 14 14 of 20 20 setups, the same as MolmoAct2-DROID and on par with the policies trained on real DROID data from this robot. On OpenYAM, it succeeds on 13 13 of 20 20 setups, while MolmoAct2, which is specifically trained on YAM, succeeds on only 7 7 . Empirically, MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM fails frequently when the object is farther from the robot compared to the receptacle, or partially hidden behind the receptacle. Despite LAP-3B’s 30% success rate on I2RT YAM, it does not succeed on OpenYAM and struggles at the pick phase.
blocks.zh: 在Franka上,OmniAct在20个设置中的14个14个成功,和MolmoAct2-DROID一样,并且与这个机器人在真正的DROID数据方面受过训练的政策相当. 在OpenYAM上,它于20个设置中的13个13个成功,而Molmo Act2则专门接受YAM训练,仅7个7个成功. 从经验来看, 与贮器相比,物体离机器人更远,或部分隐藏在贮器后面时,MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM经常发生故障。 尽管LAP-3B在I2RT YAM上取得了30%的成功率,但在OpenYAM上并没有成功,在选手阶段挣扎.

blocks.en: Notably, while UMI with all views achieves 11 / 20 11/20 on Franka, it fails on all OpenYAM setups, which fall on the edge of the training distribution. UMI (all views) receives the same training data as our model except for the scene-grounded kinematic graph ( Section 2.1 ).
blocks.zh: 值得注意的是,虽然所有观点的UMI在Franka上达到了11/20 11/20,但是它在所有OpenYAM设置上都失败了,这些设置都落在培训分发的边缘. UMI(所有视图)得到的训练数据与我们的模型相同,但根据场景绘制的运动图除外(第2.1节)。

blocks.en: 3.4 Motion strategy analysis
blocks.zh: 3.4 动议战略分析

blocks.en: During evaluation, we notice that when the object pickup site is close to the receptacle, OmniAct sometimes takes advantage of OpenYAM’s long link leading up to the gripper, simply rotating the gripper in the Z axis to reach the receptacle instead of lifting and dropping.
blocks.zh: 在评估时,我们注意到当物体拾取地点靠近贮器时,OmniAct有时会利用OpenYAM的长链路通往抓取器,只是旋转Z轴上的抓取器到达贮器,而不是起降。

blocks.en:
This is plausibly a side-effect of our data generation method: we allow for poses at different phases to have different orientations; thus, when the receptacle is close by, rotating is a viable, if not more direct, strategy. Because every trajectory in our corpus is one that its own embodiment could execute, the
data does not commit to a single grasp retargeted to different embodiments: depending on the body and the object, successful grasps approach from above, from the side, or in between. We examine whether OmniAct carries the flexibility to change its strategy depending on the embodiment and the task.
blocks.zh:
这无疑是我们数据生成方法的副作用:我们允许不同阶段的浮层具有不同的方向;因此,当贮器靠近时,旋转是一种可行、甚至更直接的战略。 因为我们身体中的每一个轨迹 都有它自己可以执行的
数据并不致力于对不同的表现形式重新进行单一的把握:视身体和物体而定,成功把握来自上方、侧面或介于两者之间。 我们审查《Omni Act》是否根据体现情况和任务而灵活地改变其战略。

blocks.en: Setup. We perform this experiment on OpenYAM, a normal-sized arm, and Lite6, an arm relatively limited in reach. A knife, a cube, and a bowl are visible. The knife lies on the surface and cannot be picked up easily from the top.
blocks.zh: 设置. 我们在OpenYAM,一个正常大小的手臂和Lite6上进行这个实验,这个手臂的伸展相对有限. 一把刀,一个立方体和一个碗是可见的. 刀身位于表面,不能轻易从顶部捡起.

blocks.en: On real tasks, OmniAct adapts its motion strategy to the task. Figure 5 (a) shows two grasps by the same OpenYAM arm from the same deployment. For the cube (top), OmniAct approaches from above and closes the gripper vertically. For the knife (bottom), it instead pitches the wrist until the gripper is level with the table and closes on the blade from the side, the orientation in which the thin body fits between the fingertips with maximum contact area. The policy treats the wrist as a free degree of freedom and picks the grasp orientation the object calls for, rather than holding a fixed top-down pose.
blocks.zh: 在实际任务上,OmniAct将其运动策略适应任务. 图5(a)显示同一OpenYAM臂从同一部署中取出的两个抓点。 对于立方体(上方),OmniAct从上方接近,并垂直关闭钳口. 对于刀(底部),它转而将手腕投向,直到抓手与桌子平齐,从侧面将刀刃紧紧地关上,即瘦身在指尖之间与最大接触区域相匹配的方向. 政策将手腕视为自由程度的自由,选择物体要求的抓取方向,而不是持有固定的自上而下姿势.

blocks.en: On real robots, OmniAct adapts its motion strategy to the embodiment. Figure 5 (b) fixes the task and varies the body. When the object is placed close to the robot, both OpenYAM and Lite6 approaches normally from the top. However, when the object is placed at the edge of Lite6’s relatively short reach (bottom), it approaches from the side with the gripper lying about 20 ∘ 20^{\circ} from the table, while on OpenYAM (top) it approaches from the top as OpenYAM can easily reach the same distance. Additionally, when attempting to pick from the side, the angles of approach are slightly different between OpenYAM and Lite6 ( Figure 5 (a)(b) bottom), such that both robots would be lying as flat as possible without putting excessive force on the table, which would trigger a gripper collision in simulation and a collision stop in real drivers.
blocks.zh: 在真正的机器人上,Omni Act将其运动策略适应于浮雕. 图5 (b) 确定任务并改变机构。 当物体被放置在机器人附近时,OpenYAM和Lite6都从顶部正常接近. 然而,当物体被放置在Lite6相对短距离(下方)的边缘时,它从侧面靠近,夹子从桌子上躺着约20 ∘ 20^{\circ},而在OpenYAM(上方)上,它从顶端靠近,因为OpenYAM可以轻松到达相同的距离. 此外,在试图从侧面选择时,OpenYAM和Lite6(图5(a)(b)底部)之间的接近角度略有不同,这样,两个机器人都会尽可能平躺,而不会把过度的力放在桌子上,从而在模拟中触发夹击碰撞,并在真正的驱动器中触发碰撞停止.

blocks.en: Overall, we can see that OmniAct adapts its motion strategy to the embodiment and the task at hand, rather than retargeting one canonical grasp across bodies and forced into an infeasible pose on one of them.
blocks.zh: 总的来说,我们可以看到,Omni Act将其运动策略适应于浮雕和手头的任务,而不是重新瞄准一个横跨身体的峡谷,并被迫对其中之一采取不可行的姿势。

blocks.en: Figure 5 : OmniAct chooses its grasp orientation for the task and the embodiment. (a) Same embodiment, different tasks: top-down for the cube, side grasp for the knife. (b) Same task, different embodiments: top-down on OpenYAM, lateral on Lite6.
blocks.zh: 图5:Omni Act选择它的任务和表现的把握方向. (a) 相同的浮雕,不同的任务:立方体的自上而下,刀的侧抓。 (b) 任务相同,表现不同:OpenYAM上下,Lite6上横向。

blocks.zh: 3.5 阅读研究

Success falls monotonically: − 6.5 % -6.5\% at one half, and − 26.8 % -26.8\% at one eighth, on a 500 rollout step limit.

Removing the exocentric views as well, leaving only wrist observations, costs a further 36.8 % 36.8\% .

blocks.en: 4 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en: We find that scaling diverse robotic embodiments and supplying scene-grounded kinematic graphs lead to better generalization to unseen robots on real-world tasks, enabling body-specific motion strategies for the task at hand. Scaling the number of training embodiments drives performance on held-out simulated embodiments. The scene-grounded kinematic graph provides a small amount of improvement as well, but farther away from the training distribution, the graph’s contribution appears much larger ( e.g . OpenYAM). These results suggest that embodiment scale covers bodies that resemble the training ones, while the graph carries the policy to a body at the edge of that distribution.
blocks.zh: 我们发现,扩大各种机器人的化身和提供场景动能图,可以更好地将现实世界任务中的机器人概括为看不见的机器人,从而能够为手头的任务制定具体的身体运动战略。 增加培训的化身数量将推动在模拟化的化身上的表现。 以场景为背景的动画图也提供了少量的改进,但离培训分布更远,图中的贡献似乎要大得多(例如OpenYAM). 这些结果表明,体现比例表涵盖与培训类似的机构,而图表将政策带给分布边缘的机构。

blocks.en: An open question is to scale embodiments types further, including bimanual arms, humanoids, and everyday objects such as tools, equipment, and vehicles.
blocks.zh: 一个尚未解决的问题是进一步扩大浮雕的种类,包括双人武器、人品以及工具、设备和车辆等日常物品。
